stories.title: Skin Care Brand FaceGym to Open New Tribeca Location at 110 Reade Street
stories.excerpt: Time to face the music. FaceGym, a skin care brand that describes itself as a “facial fitness” studio, has inked a 10-year, 2,400-square-foot lease for a new Tribeca spot at 110 Reade Street, according to landlord broker Platinum Commercial. Founded in 2014 in London, FaceGym offers customers “facial workouts” and “combines muscle manipulation techniques” to provide lifting and sculpting services without surgery, according to its website. The brand has 15 locations globally, including four others in New York City on the Upper East Side, in NoHo and in Midtown. “The strongest retail brands today are making long-term investments in neighborhoods that complement their identity and where they can build lasting relationships with their customers,” Platinum Commercial’s Steven Evans, who repped the landlord, said in a statement. “Tribeca has evolved into one of Manhattan’s premier destinations for luxury wellness, beauty and experiential retail, attracting brands that value authenticity, quality and community. FaceGym is an ideal addition to that ecosystem.” The asking rent was $110 per square foot. The new location is expected to open this month. Isaacs and Company represented the tenant, but the names of the brokers who represented the tenant were not immediately available. Built in 1861 near the corner of Reade Street and West Broadway, 110 Reade Street is a six-story, mixed-use residential property with ground-floor retail. Fitness studio Pure Barre was a former tenant in the retail space. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: FaceGym signs 10-year, 2,400-SF lease at 110 Reade Street, Tribeca.
Brand has 15 global locations; four others already in NYC metro.
Tribeca positioning as luxury wellness/beauty retail destination for experiential brands.
stories.summary: FaceGym, a London-founded facial fitness studio, has leased 2,400 square feet in Tribeca for 10 years as part of expansion across four NYC locations. The brand joins a wave of experiential wellness and beauty retailers clustering in Manhattan's premium neighborhoods. Tribeca's evolution into a luxury wellness hub reflects broader retail repositioning post-pandemic.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development. However, the clustering of experiential retail and wellness brands in Tribeca signals affluent, experience-driven demographics that could support higher-rent residential units in the neighborhood; this underlines Tribeca's continued appeal to high-income renters and supports valuation assumptions for nearby multifamily assets.

stories.title: SMBC Refis Apartments near Dallas, Philly With $108M Loan
stories.excerpt: The Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys are longtime fierce rivals in the National Football League’s NFC East, but the two markets have a common link in one of commercial real estate’s latest multifamily financings. Ares Real Estate has inked a $107.5 million loan to refinance an apartment portfolio in the Dallas-Fort Worth and Philadelphia areas that together include nearly 600 units, Commercial Observer can first report. Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC) provided the loan for Ares’ Axis 110 property in Richardson, Texas, and for Skye 750 in King of Prussia, Pa. CBRE arranged the transaction with a global institutional debt advisory group consisting of Tom Traynor, Tom Rugg, Peter Griesinger, Arman Samouk and Kayla Kaloostian. The 2017-built Axis 110 at 110 W CityLine Drive in Richardson has 351 apartments next to the Dallas Area Rapid Transit CityLine Station. Resident amenities include a swimming pool, a skyline terrace, a fitness center and 8,110 square feet of ground-floor retail. Skye 750, at 750 Moore Road 20 miles northwest from Philadelphia, was completed in 2019 with 248 units. Its amenities include a swimming pool, a fire pit, a dog park, coworking space, a health club and a sauna. SMBC did not immediately return a request for comment. Ares declined to comment Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: SMBC provides $107.5M refi for 600-unit portfolio across Dallas-Fort Worth and Philadelphia.
Axis 110 (351 units, Richardson, TX near DART CityLine); Skye 750 (PA), both stabilized.
Transit-adjacent Dallas asset and suburban Philly property attract institutional debt at scale.
stories.summary: Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation has refinanced a two-property, nearly 600-unit multifamily portfolio for Ares Real Estate, comprising Axis 110 in Richardson, Texas (351 units, 2017-built, near DART transit) and Skye 750 in King of Prussia, Pennsylvania (circa 250 units). The $107.5M loan reflects strong lender appetite for stabilized product in secondary markets with transit access and suburban office/mixed-use anchors.
stories.impact: Refinance activity and institutional debt appetite for DFW and Philadelphia multifamily signal sustained capital availability and confidence in both metros' rental fundamentals. Axis 110's transit-oriented location near DART CityLine validates developer thesis that suburban Dallas infill near employment nodes and transit commands refinance capital; similar positioning could accelerate development starts in DFW suburbs. Philly's inclusion suggests suburban Philly rental markets (King of Prussia submarket) remain attractive to capital despite regional office headwinds.

stories.title: Alliance Building 10th Charlotte Rental Community
stories.excerpt: Alliance Residential Co. will break ground before the end of this year on Broadstone Enderly Park, a 336-unit community at 1306 Berryhill Road. It will be the company’s 10th apartment project in the Charlotte metro area. The Charlotte Business Journal reports that Alliance acquired the 3.39-acre site from Beacon Partners and Browder Brown for $13.5 million. Unit sizes will average out at 800 square feet. Amenities will include a pool, multiple outdoor kitchens with grilling areas, open green space, package room, dog park and pet-washing station. The property’s clubhouse will house the leasing office, fitness center, club and game rooms and co-working offices. Cline Design Associates is the project architect. The project is expected to begin delivering units some time in 2028. Alliance’s most recent Charlotte delivery was Broadstone West End, a five-story, 332-unit apartment community at 2220 Wilkinson Blvd. The development opened in summer 2025. It also delivered Matheson Mill by Broadstone, a 302-unit community at 120 Matheson Ave. near NoDa, in April 2025. The post Alliance Building 10th Charlotte Rental Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Alliance Residential to break ground in 2025 on Broadstone Enderly Park (336 units) in Charlotte.
Project is developer's 10th Charlotte community; $13.5M land acquisition from Beacon Partners.
Delivery expected 2028; two recent Alliance Charlotte deliveries (2025): 332 and 302 units.
stories.summary: Alliance Residential has acquired a 3.39-acre Charlotte site for $13.5 million and will break ground before year-end on Broadstone Enderly Park, a 336-unit community with average 800-SF units and full amenity package. This marks Alliance's 10th Charlotte project; the company delivered two properties totaling 634 units in spring/summer 2025, demonstrating aggressive Charlotte pipeline execution.
stories.impact: Charlotte's sustained multifamily supply pipeline—with Alliance alone delivering 634 units in 2025 and breaking ground on 336 more—signals strong development confidence and likely robust rental demand absorption. Rapid consecutive deliveries (West End summer 2025, Matheson Mill April 2025, Enderly Park 2028) and reacquisition velocity indicate Charlotte's job growth and in-migration are outpacing supply, supporting sub-market rent growth and continued developer appetite. Monitor absorption and rent trends in Berryhill Road submarket post-Enderly Park delivery to gauge market saturation.

stories.title: Limited Fort Lauderdale Office Deliveries Tighten Market
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap (NYSE: MMI) published its fourth quarter 2026 Fort Lauderdale Office Market Report. Deliveries are down, vacancy rates are falling, and rents are up, all good signs for Fort Lauderdale office investors. Key findings include: Several established office corridors are holding up well, with Cypress Creek vacancy falling 280 basis points year-over-year to 14.7 percent and Hollywood declining 90 basis points to 16.3 percent. New office deliveries remain limited, with T3 FAT Village the only significant traditional office project slated for 2026 and its 341,500 square feet of Class A space fully available as of June. Average asking rents rose 5.3 percent year-over-year to nearly $28 per square foot in June, as newer office properties continued to attract tenants willing to pay higher rents. Office investment pricing is showing signs of stabilization, with average sale pricing reaching nearly $320 per square foot for the year ended June and 2026 transactions concentrated in well-occupied, stabilized Class B assets. The post Limited Fort Lauderdale Office Deliveries Tighten Market appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Fort Lauderdale office deliveries down; vacancy falling and rents rising (Q4 2026).
Limited new office supply tightening market conditions for existing stock.
No direct multifamily data; office market dynamics suggest broader market strength.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap's fourth-quarter 2026 Fort Lauderdale Office Market Report shows declining deliveries, falling vacancy rates, and rising rents. The tightening supply and demand balance reflect limited new office construction and stable demand.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance. However, Fort Lauderdale office market tightening (fewer deliveries, lower vacancy, rising rents) signals sustained corporate demand and employment stability in South Florida, which supports longer-term multifamily rental demand tailwinds. Office supply constraints may redirect corporate real estate spending into workforce amenities (including employee housing subsidies) and attract talent-dependent firms to the region, modestly reinforcing multifamily fundamentals.

stories.title: CREW Network unveils strategic plan built on four priorities
stories.excerpt: Shaped by five months of member input, the plan puts women at the center of commercial real estate’s biggest shifts CREW Network, which has more than 14,000 members and 90 chapters, has introduced a strategic plan built on four priorities (Connection, Advancement, Influence and Access) designed to help women lead change in commercial real estate rather than simply keep pace with it. The plan arrives as the industry navigates shifts ranging from artificial intelligence to the need to invest in a new generation of leaders. More than a refreshed mission statement, the plan is focused on business outcomes: deals, wealth-building and leadership seats, Alison Beddard, CEO of CREW Network, said during a Sept. 24 interview at the 2026 CREW Network Convention in Miami, Florida. “When women rise, everyone rises; that belief drives every choice in this plan,” Beddard said. Here is how each of the four priorities puts that belief into practice. 1. Connection The first priority is to deepen the value of networking, so every member connection leads to tangible business outcomes. For CREW, that means treating relationships as a source of deals and growth, not as an end in themselves. “From across the street to across the globe, CREW gives you the network to elevate your business,” said Beddard, who before becoming CREW CEO, spent two decades with Cushman & Wakefield, most recently as managing principal for the firm’s Washington and Oregon markets. 2. Advancement The second priority is to accelerate the careers and professional growth of all women in commercial real estate. Advancement is tied to real results, including leadership seats and wealth-building. “I want every member in CREW to rise as far and as fast as their ambition will take them,” Beddard said. 3. Influence The third priority is to position CREW and its members as the premier thought leader and the most inclusive business network in the industry. bullets: CREW Network (14K+ members, 90 chapters) unveils strategic plan on Connection, Advancement, Influence, Access.
Focus on tangible business outcomes: deals, wealth-building, leadership seats for women in CRE.
Plan addresses industry shifts (AI, generational leadership) and diversity in commercial real estate.
stories.summary: CREW Network, a 14,000-member, 90-chapter women's commercial real estate organization, has launched a strategic plan centered on four priorities: Connection, Advancement, Influence, and Access. The initiative emphasizes measurable business outcomes (deals, wealth-building, leadership) rather than networking alone, and responds to industry challenges including AI integration and generational leadership gaps.
stories.impact: No material direct impact to multifamily development markets or capital flows. CREW's strategic refocus on deal flow and wealth-building may marginally increase women's deal participation and leadership visibility in multifamily development, but does not affect supply, demand, capital availability, or construction cost fundamentals. Relevant only to firms prioritizing diversity metrics in investment and development teams.

stories.title: Netflix Studios Extends Nearly 10K-SF Lease at 817 Broadway
stories.excerpt: A major streaming platform has renewed its office space just south of Manhattan’s Union Square, Commercial Observer has learned. Netflix Studios extended its lease spanning 9,943 square feet at Taconic Partners’ 817 Broadway, according to a source with knowledge of the deal. It’s unclear when the tenant moved in or how long the extension is for. Asking rent for the space was $115 per square foot. CBRE’s Charles Laginestra and Rocco Laginestra negotiated on behalf of the landlord, while Newmark‘s David Falk, Jason Greenstein, Daniel Levine and Jordyn Comras represented Netflix in the deal. CBRE did not immediately respond to a request for comment, while Newmark declined to comment. Other tenants in the building constructed in 1895 include Paris-based crypto company Ledger, which signed a 3,437-square-foot lease in March, and development platform Unity Technologies, which took 10,000 square feet in August 2025. Around this time last year, GreenBarn Investment Group and Sabal Investment Holdings led a $128.5 million recapitalization of the 14-story, Class A office property on Broadway, which at the time was fully leased before SDC Capital Partners relocated from the building in July. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Netflix Studios extends ~10K-SF lease at 817 Broadway, Manhattan (south of Union Square).
Other recent tenants: Ledger (crypto, 3.4K SF, March), Unity Technologies (10K SF, Aug 2025).
Building recapitalized for $128.5M in 2025; Class A office on prime Broadway corridor.
stories.summary: Netflix has renewed its 9,943-square-foot lease at Taconic Partners' 817 Broadway, a Class A, 1895-built office building south of Union Square in Manhattan. The building also houses Ledger (crypto) and Unity Technologies (development platform), and underwent a $128.5M recapitalization in 2025.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Netflix's lease renewal signals continued office demand from mega-cap media/tech companies in lower Manhattan, but does not directly affect rental housing supply, demand, or capital flows. However, persistent streaming/media company anchors in Manhattan office suggest some resilience in premium office submarkets, which may indirectly support affluent renter profiles in nearby residential buildings (Union Square area multifamily assets).

stories.title: BXP Sells 11% Stake in 343 Madison Avenue Office Tower to AVRS Partners
stories.excerpt: BXP, the largest Class A office owner in the country, has sold a 10.6 percent stake in 343 Madison Avenue, a planned 46-story, 930,000-square-foot office development in Midtown Manhattan that is expected to cost roughly $2 billion, to AVRS Partners. “We are pleased and honored to expand our relationship with AVRS Partners through this investment,” BXP Chairman and CEO Owen Thomas said in a statement. AVRS, which was founded by Edmond M. Safra in 2023, also owns equity stakes in 77 Water Street in Manhattan’s Financial District and also in One Willoughby Square, Brooklyn’s tallest office tower. This is not the first deal between BXP and AVRS: The firms share ownership in the General Motors Building at 767 Fifth Avenue in Manhattan, an office property valued at $3.7 billion, according to recent filings by BXP. “BXP has been a valued partner to my family for more than a decade,” Safra said in a statement. “I’m honored that AVRS is now building on that relationship, and we look forward to the development of 343 Madison Avenue.” The equity infusion from ABRS comes just weeks after Commercial Observer reported BXP secured $1.2 billion in construction financing for 343 Madison Avenue from Wells Fargo, Bank of America Securities, Bank of New York Mellon and J.P. Morgan Chase. Sitting just west of Grand Central Terminal between East 44th Street and 45th Street, 343 Madison is in the heart of the Midtown office corridor, near iconic office towers such as One Vanderbilt and the MetLife Building at 200 Park Avenue. 343 Madison Avenue has not yet begun construction but has already secured several strong leases. C.V. Starr signed a 275,000-square-foot deal in October to anchor the property, and law firm McDermott Will & Schulte took roughly 150,000 square feet there in April. bullets: BXP sells 10.6% stake in 343 Madison Avenue (46-story, 930K-SF, $2B Midtown office tower) to AVRS Partners.
AVRS (founded 2023 by Edmond Safra) already owns stakes in 77 Water Street (FiDi), One Willoughby (Brooklyn).
BXP and AVRS co-own GM Building ($3.7B); partnership expanding across premium Manhattan office.
stories.summary: Boston Properties has sold a 10.6% equity stake in the planned 46-story, 930,000-square-foot, $2 billion 343 Madison Avenue office tower to AVRS Partners, a 2023-founded investment vehicle backed by Edmond Safra. AVRS already holds equity in 77 Water Street and One Willoughby Square, and co-owns the $3.7B General Motors Building with BXP.
stories.impact: No direct multifamily impact. However, BXP's capital recycling (selling stakes in new development) may signal portfolio rebalancing or capital deployment constraints, while AVRS's aggressive accumulation of premium Manhattan office suggests investor confidence in Class A recovery and supply scarcity. The $2B 343 Madison Avenue development reinforces Midtown's continued appeal to ultra-institutional capital despite office headwinds; sustained office investment concentrates corporate tenant demand and high-income professional populations that support rental housing demand in Midtown/CBD submarkets.

stories.title: UF Site for New 684-Bed Student Housing Community
stories.excerpt: 908 Group has broken ground on Chapter House UF, a 684-bed, Class A student housing community at 920 SW Depot Ave., adjacent to the University of Florida campus. The project is being developed in partnership with Batson-Cook Development Company (BCDC), with construction financing from Pacific Life. Chapter House UF marks 908 Group’s fifth joint venture with BCDC, and its fourth construction loan with Pacific Life. The project will include 219 units totaling 684 beds, more than 9,000 square feet of amenity space and a structured parking garage. Completion will occur summer prior to the Fall 2028 academic year. ARCO/Murray is serving as general contractor, Humphreys & Partners Architects is the architect . With more than 57,000 students enrolled at UF and record-high application demand, the market continues to attract long-term institutional investment. 908 Group recently delivered another UF-area student housing community. The post UF Site for New 684-Bed Student Housing Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 908 Group/BCDC break ground on Chapter House UF (684 beds, 219 units) in Gainesville, Florida.
UF enrollment 57K+, record-high applications; project completes summer prior to Fall 2028 semester.
Fifth JV with BCDC, fourth loan with Pacific Life; recent UF delivery also completed.
stories.summary: 908 Group and Batson-Cook Development Company have broken ground on Chapter House UF, a Class A, 684-bed student housing community (219 units) adjacent to the University of Florida campus, financed by Pacific Life. UF enrollment exceeds 57,000 with record application demand; delivery targeted for summer 2028 to meet Fall semester occupancy.
stories.impact: Strong demand signal for Gainesville student housing. Record UF applications and 57K+ enrollment support robust student housing fundamentals and justify continued institutional development investment. Rapid sequential institutional capital deployment (908/BCDC repeat partnership, Pacific Life's fourth loan) validates supply absorption and rent stability in the market. However, repeat builds and high institutional focus suggest potential near-term supply pipeline acceleration; monitor future Gainesville student housing deliveries and absorption velocity to gauge oversupply risk post-2028.

stories.title: Link Logistics Offloads 1.1M-SF Alpharetta Warehouse Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Lincoln Property Company acquired Shiloh Light Industrial Portfolio, a 1,085,294-square-foot, ten-building Class A light industrial portfolio located in the Atlanta metropolitan area in Alpharetta, Georgia. Link Logistics (a Blackstone portfolio company) was the seller. Built between 1995 and 2000, the portfolio consists of ten buildings. The portfolio is currently 100% leased to 21 tenants engaged in last-mile logistics, light manufacturing and specialty distribution. Lincoln has plans to convert the single-tenant space to multi-tenant configurations and modernize the buildings. Known locally as Atlanta’s “Technology Corridor,” the submarket’s demographics make it a natural fit for last-mile logistics, light manufacturing and specialty distribution tenants. Forsyth County’s population has grown at nearly five times the U.S. average over the past five years, and Fulton County’s growth has been almost double the national rate. Lincoln was awarded the transaction in August 2026, marking the fourth acquisition in Lincoln Logistics Fund II. The post Link Logistics Offloads 1.1M-SF Alpharetta Warehouse Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Lincoln Property acquires Shiloh Light Industrial Portfolio (1.1M SF, 10 buildings) in Alpharetta from Link Logistics (Blackstone).
100% leased to 21 tenants (last-mile, light manufacturing, specialty distribution); built 1995-2000.
Forsyth County population growth ~5X U.S. average; Fulton County ~2X; submarket is 'Technology Corridor.'
stories.summary: Lincoln Property Company has acquired the Shiloh Light Industrial Portfolio (1,085,294 square feet, ten Class A buildings) in Alpharetta, Georgia from Blackstone's Link Logistics. The portfolio is 100% leased across 21 tenants in last-mile logistics, light manufacturing, and specialty distribution. Lincoln plans to reposition single-tenant space to multi-tenant configurations; the Atlanta Technology Corridor submarket has experienced population growth at 5X the U.S. rate (Forsyth) and 2X nationally (Fulton).
stories.impact: Indirect signal of robust Atlanta metro employment fundamentals and logistics/manufacturing clustering in north Atlanta suburbs. Forsyth/Alpharetta population growth at 5X U.S. average creates strong rental housing demand tailwinds; logistics/tech tenant concentration attracts younger, mobile workforces that drive multifamily absorption. Lincoln's repositioning strategy (single-to-multi-tenant) signals supply chain and last-mile convergence driving need for flexible industrial space, which attracts high-wage distribution and tech talent to Alpharetta submarket. Monitor multifamily deliveries in Alpharetta/North Fulton corridors to capitalize on worker in-migration; submarket remains undersupplied relative to employer/logistics node density.

stories.title: CMBS Loan Backed by Hyatt Regency Waikiki Beach Resort Sent to Special Servicing
stories.excerpt: A $302 million commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) loan secured by the Hyatt Regency Waikiki Beach Resort & Spa, a 1,230-key luxury resort in Honolulu, has been sent to special servicing after sponsorship failed to deliver its final maturity payment earlier this month, according to an alert from Morningstar Credit. The $302 million loan — listed as HONO 2021-LULU, a single-asset, single-borrower CMBS loan — is the remaining debt on a $450 million loan owner Mirae Asset Global Investments Company, a South Korean-based asset management firm, used to refinance the property in 2021. The four-star hotel was in negotiations to be sold when the maturity default occurred, per special servicer commentary. Located at 2424 Kalākaua Avenue in Honolulu, Hawaii, the Hyatt Regency Waikiki Beach opened in 1976 and is structured as a two-tower luxury resort with approximately 94,961 square feet of retail space on site. Cash flow has been a problem for the property. The 2021-vintage CMBS loan was underwritten for $36.7 million of annual revenue, but exceeded no more than $25.9 million in 2023. Mirae purchased the property from Blackstone in September 2016 for $780 million. Bloomberg reported last year that Mirae expected to sell the hotel for as low as $650 million. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Hyatt Regency Waikiki Beach Resort ($302M CMBS loan) sent to special servicing after maturity default.
2021 refinance ($450M original) for $36.7M underwritten revenue; 2023 actual: $25.9M (29% shortfall).
Property in sales negotiations; cash flow distress driven by demand/rate environment post-pandemic.
stories.summary: A $302 million single-asset CMBS loan secured by the Hyatt Regency Waikiki Beach Resort & Spa (1,230 keys, Honolulu) has been sent to special servicing after the sponsor failed to make its final maturity payment. The 2021 refinance was underwritten for $36.7M annual revenue but generated only $25.9M in 2023 (29% decline). The property was in sales negotiations at the time of default.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. However, Hyatt Waikiki's maturity default and revenue collapse signal distress in hospitality-adjacent real estate and broader refinance headwinds for tourism-dependent assets in 2025-2026. If interest rates remain elevated or travel demand remains pressure-tested, similar cash flow stress could emerge in mixed-use or hospitality-anchored developments; multifamily developers with mixed-use aspirations should stress-test hotel/hospitality components aggressively. No material impact to core multifamily fundamentals unless Waikiki distress signals broader Hawaii rental market weakness (unlikely, given strong tourism dependence).
